description:
Monterrei Castle rises above the Támega river valley, dominating the historic border between Spain and Portugal. It is made up of three walled enclosures that include the Renaissance-style Palace of the Counts and the Keep and Ladies' towers. Throughout its history it served very different functions: medieval castle, manor house, military barracks, and even a pilgrim hospital.

Following a complete rehabilitation, the Parador opened its doors in 2015, offering today a fusion of the complex's history with modern comforts. Accommodation is split between the former Palace of the Counts (7 rooms) and the Casa Rectoral (5 rooms), both within the walled enclosure.

The castle's varied historical uses — from military stronghold to pilgrim hospital — give Monterrei a functional range unusual among Spain's castle-hotels, most of which served either purely military or purely residential purposes.

Widely considered by historians to be Galicia's largest acropolis, the complex's three separate walled enclosures give it a scale distinct from the single-building fortresses found elsewhere in the region.

The castle's position directly on the historic Spain-Portugal border gives guests staying at Monterrei a specific frontier-zone setting within Galicia.

hotel.how_to_stay:
**Getting there:** In Monterrei, Province of Ourense, Galicia, on the historic Spain-Portugal border.

**Rooms & rates:** Rooms split between the former Palace of the Counts (7 rooms) and the Casa Rectoral (5 rooms), both within the walled enclosure; from about €114 per night.

**On-site:** Restaurant (Marmitia), setting within the three walled enclosures with views over the Támega valley.

**Good to know:** One of the newest Paradores in the network (2015), and historically it also functioned as a pilgrim hospital — a little-known detail.

**Combine with:** Verín and the wider Támega valley border region.
